- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the mid-to-late period of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show early upward bias but fail to capture sharp spikes or late-period volatility.
- After a spike in true values, forecasts often overshoot and then gradually decay — suggesting lag in adjusting to new regime.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled; forecasts remain flat or slowly trending while true values exhibit strong momentum.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture sudden drops or sharp rises in the last 5–10 days.
- Model exhibits “late-period bias” — underestimates true values in the final 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts are too conservative in the early days, then gradually increase — but miss the true peak or trough that occurs later.
- Model fails to adjust to recent high volatility; underestimates risk premium or supply-demand shifts in the final 10 days.
- Forecasts often lag behind true values by 3–5 days, especially after a spike or correction.
- Model does not account for “rebound” or “reversal” patterns after a sharp drop — tends to underestimate recovery.
